newsitem.title: FINLAND: Finnish funds see '97 assets growing to FIM 20 bln.
newsitem.headline: Finnish funds see '97 assets growing to FIM 20 bln.

text.p: The Finnish mutual fund association said on Thursday it expected 1997 to be another good year and saw assets invested in mutual funds growing to 20 billion markka from 11.6 billion at end-1996.
"Growth could be close to 20 billion markka," association chairman Mikael Schroder told a news conference.

Funds expected shares on the Helsinki bourse to appreciate this year, too, but the heady 50 percent rise of 1996 is unlikely to repeat itself, said Mikko Savikko, managing director of the association.
"We will hardly see another 50 percent rise," he said.
The return on investment in stock funds was 49.9 percent on average last year, Savikko said, but added that investors had -- if anything -- fled stock funds during the year.
"Although the return on stock funds has been most profitable in the long-run, investing in stock funds can be risky in the near-term due to uncertainty factors from overseas," he said.
Assets in Finnish mutual funds more than doubled last year to 11.6 billion markka from 5.2 billion a year earlier.
Money market funds, investing mainly in short-term maturities, held 43 percent of assets in funds registered in Finland in 1996, and stock funds accounted for 24 percent.
Mutual funds investing in bonds had a 20 percent share and so called balance funds, placing assets in a mix of instruments, accounted for 13 percent, the association said.
At the end of 1995, stock funds had 43 percent of total assets in mutual funds, bond funds 24 percent, balance funds 19 percent and short-money funds just six percent.
The association expected that this year the growth would be spread more evenly between different kinds of funds.
